Saccharine

SAK-uh-rin · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Saccharine is excessively sweet, either in literal taste or in an insincere, overly emotional way.

The greeting card aisle was full of saccharine verses about love that felt more like a sales pitch than a real sentiment.

Worked Example

The best man's saccharine toast, dripping with rehearsed compliments and staged tears, made the groom visibly cringe.

The toast wasn't a simple, warm tribute -- it was so overloaded with sweetness and forced emotion that it felt fake, which is exactly what saccharine describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

cloying: excessively sweet or sentimental, to an unpleasant degree

syrupy: excessively sweet or sentimental

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

bitter: having a sharp, unpleasant taste; also, harsh in tone

sincere: genuine and heartfelt, not exaggerated

Where it sits · how far past pleasant it goes — sweet → saccharine → sickening

sweet vs. saccharine: Something merely sweet is pleasant, without the excessive, almost sickly quality of something saccharine.

sickening vs. saccharine: Something sickening is so overwhelming it turns the stomach, an even more extreme reaction than a saccharine song might cause.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — sacchar-

root — sacchar-: sugar (from Greek sakkharon, by way of Latin saccharum)

suffix — -ine

suffix — -ine: having the nature of (Latin -inus)

Put it together

Put it together: Saccharine is built from sacchar- ('sugar,' from Greek sakkharon, by way of Latin saccharum) + -ine ('having the nature of') -- 'having the nature of sugar.' The same root gives us the chemistry term saccharide, the name for a sugar molecule.

Use the root in a new word: saccharide

Use the root in a new word: saccharide: A polysaccharide is a large molecule made of many simple sugar units linked together.

Word Choice

Saccharine is almost always a criticism -- it describes sweetness pushed so far that it feels fake or unpleasant, whether in a dessert, a song, or an overly emotional story.
